evidence: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING with LINKAGE SECTION parameters

purpose.summary: A called subprogram (CWXTDATE) that performs two date-related calculations: (1) computing an employee's years of service by comparing hire date to run date, and (2) determining whether the run date is the last day of the month (end-of-month indicator), including leap-year handling for February. It is part of a Compuware Xpediter/TSO COBOL demo/training suite.

notable_features: LINKAGE SECTION with four parameters passed via PROCEDURE DIVISION USING
REDEFINES clause on DATE-TABLE to create an OCCURS 12 TIMES table for month/day lookup
88-level condition name used as a switch (CHECKED-FOR-EOM)
GOBACK instead of STOP RUN (subprogram pattern)
Sequence numbers embedded in source lines (e.g. '11032000') indicating mainframe source management
Intentional bug in 3000-CALC-LEAP-YEAR: DIVIDE BY 0 (likely a training exercise to demonstrate debugging with Xpediter)
verdict.notes: The DIVIDE RUN-YY BY 0 in paragraph 3000-CALC-LEAP-YEAR is almost certainly an intentional bug inserted for Xpediter/TSO debugging training purposes (should be DIVIDE 4 INTO RUN-YY for leap-year check). The program is otherwise well-structured. Sequence numbers visible at columns 73-80 on some lines confirm mainframe fixed-format origin.
